q-64967.:question/problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $y=1.$ Given that the point $P$ with $x$-coordinate $\pi $ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=y{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
q-64967.:question/worked-solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=1.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point where $x=\pi $ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(\pi ,1).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(\pi ,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(\pi ,1) & =(1){e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 1) \\  & ={e}^{0}(-1) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
